newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - fuel, gas oil firm, others not.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - fuel, gas oil firm, others not.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Friday. Gasoline was weaker with little demand and relatively good supply of product, traders said.
One dealer was heard looking for 25,000 tonnes of mixed grades of gasoline for Lebanon, but few other buyers were on the horizon.
Offers of low octane barrels were seen out of Italy and little product was expected to move northwards because of similar prices either side of Gibraltar.
Naphtha was weaker with crude. An Indian cargo was heard having passed through the region on its way to an end user in NWE, and Suez and Libyan cargoes were also thought to be available.
Gas oil was firm but traders said the market was unsettled as key players returned from holiday and assessed positions ahead of the autumn and the introduction of EU low sulphur diesel regulations.
Premiums on prompt Russian material were under pressure but seen strengthening into September.
A Norwegian refiner was looking for a cargo into Slovenia for Sept 1-10 delivery and bidding at quotes cif high +$2.0 per tonne, basis Genoa, traders said. Offers were put at quotes cif high +$2.5.
There was talk of ex-storage material offered out of Malta at quotes fob high +$4.0.
There was also talk of an Italian islands cargo trading roughly quotes cif high +$1.0 to $1.25.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil was firm, but quiet on the physical market with the exception of Portugal's EdP tendering to buy six cargoes in September with an option for a further two in October. The tender, which will be awarded on Aug 30, boosted swaps levels by 50-75 cent and was expected to give support to wet barrels.
A dealer was offering a second half September 30,000 tonne ISAB cargo and rejecting bis of fob Med +$1.
The straight run market was very tight for both low and high sulphur material.
